statements.subject: imap
statements.description: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: "RFC822" should be interpreted as a reference to the updated [RFC5322] standard.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: the client SHOULD generate a unique tag for every command, but a server MUST accept tag reuse.
actions: generate unique tag for each command

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST follow the syntax outlined in this specification strictly.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In all cases, the client MUST send a complete command (including receiving all command continuation request responses and sending command continuations for the command) before initiating a new command.
actions: receive all command continuation request responses
send command continuations for the current command
defer new command initiation until current command is complete

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server data MAY be sent as a result of a client command or MAY be sent unilaterally by the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD strictly enforce the syntax outlined in this specification.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any client command with a protocol syntax error, including (but not limited to) missing or extraneous spaces or arguments, SHOULD be rejected and the client given a BAD server completion response.
actions: reject client command
send BAD completion response to client

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MUST be prepared to accept any server response at all times.
actions: accept server response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Server data SHOULD be remembered (cached), so that the client can reference its remembered copy rather than sending a command to the server to request the data.
actions: cache received server data

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In the case of certain server data, the data MUST be remembered, as specified elsewhere in this document.
actions: remember specified server data

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A UID is an unsigned non-zero 32-bit value assigned to each message, which when used with the unique identifier validity value (see below) forms a 64-bit value that MUST NOT refer to any other message in the mailbox or any subsequent mailbox with the same name forever.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The unique identifier of a message MUST NOT change during the session and SHOULD NOT change between sessions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Any change of unique identifiers between sessions MUST be detectable using the UIDVALIDITY mechanism discussed below.
actions: expose UID change via UIDVALIDITY

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Unless the unique identifier validity also changes (see below), the next unique identifier value MUST have the following two characteristics.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: First, the next unique identifier value MUST NOT change unless new messages are added to the mailbox; and second, the next unique identifier value MUST change whenever new messages are added to the mailbox, even if those new messages are subsequently expunged.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If unique identifiers from an earlier session fail to persist in this session, the unique identifier validity value MUST be greater than the one used in the earlier session.
actions: assign UIDVALIDITY greater than previous session value

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: Ideally, unique identifiers SHOULD persist at all times.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Unique identifiers MUST be strictly ascending in the mailbox at all times.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the physical message store is reordered by a non-IMAP agent, the unique identifiers in the mailbox MUST be regenerated, since the former unique identifiers are no longer strictly ascending as a result of the reordering.
actions: regenerate unique identifiers to restore strictly ascending order

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In particular, the internal date, RFC822.SIZE, envelope, body structure, and message texts (all BODY[...] fetch data items) MUST never change.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a message is expunged, its UID MUST NOT be reused under the same UIDVALIDITY value.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This position MUST be ordered by ascending unique identifiers.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MAY permit the client to define new keywords in the mailbox (see the description of the PERMANENTFLAGS response code for more information).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These keywords SHOULD be supported (allowed in SEARCH and allowed and preserved in APPEND, COPY, and MOVE commands) by server implementations:

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Once set, the flag SHOULD NOT be cleared.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If more than one of these is set for a message, the client MUST treat it as if none are set, and it SHOULD unset both of them on the IMAP server.
actions: treat $Junk and $NotJunk flags as if neither is set

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: New keywords SHOULD be registered in this registry using the procedure specified in [RFC5788].

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In the case of messages created by the IMAP4rev2 COPY or MOVE command, this SHOULD be the same as the Internal Date attribute of the source message.
actions: Set Internal Date of newly created message equal to Internal Date of source message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In the case of messages created by the IMAP4rev2 APPEND command, this SHOULD be the date and time as specified in the APPEND command description.
actions: Set Internal Date of newly appended message to the date and time specified in the APPEND command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This size SHOULD match the result of a "FETCH BODY[]" command.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In the not authenticated state, the client MUST supply authentication credentials before most commands will be permitted.
actions: supply authentication credentials before issuing commands

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In the authenticated state, the client is authenticated and MUST select a mailbox to access before commands that affect messages will be permitted.
actions: select a mailbox before commands that affect messages are permitted

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client requests the logout state, the server MUST send an untagged BYE response and a tagged OK response to the LOGOUT command before the server closes the connection; and the client MUST read the tagged OK response to the LOGOUT command before the client closes the connection.
actions: send untagged BYE response
send tagged OK response to LOGOUT command
close connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT unilaterally close the connection without first sending an untagged BYE response that contains the reason for doing so.
actions: send untagged BYE response containing reason for closing
close connection

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD NOT unilaterally close the connection; instead, it SHOULD issue a LOGOUT command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server detects that the client has unilaterally closed the connection, the server MAY omit the untagged BYE response and simply close its connection.
actions: omit untagged BYE response
close server connection

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In the case of synchronizing literals transmitted from client to server, the client MUST wait to receive a command continuation request (described later in this document) before sending the octet data (and the remainder of the command).
actions: suspend octet data transmission
await command continuation request before sending octet data and remainder of command

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The non-synchronizing literal is an alternative form of synchronizing literal and may be used from client to server anywhere a synchronizing literal is permitted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The non-synchronizing literal form MUST NOT be sent from server to client.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The server does not generate a command continuation request in response to a non-synchronizing literal, and clients are not required to wait before sending the octets of a non-synchronizing literal.
actions: may send octet data immediately without awaiting command continuation request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Unless otherwise specified in an IMAP extension, non-synchronizing literals MUST NOT be larger than 4096 octets.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any literal larger than 4096 bytes MUST be sent as a synchronizing literal.
actions: send literal as synchronizing literal

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Even if the octet count is 0, a client transmitting a synchronizing literal MUST wait to receive a command continuation request.
actions: wait for command continuation request before sending octet data

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: IMAP4rev2 implementations MAY transmit 8-bit or multi-octet characters in literals but SHOULD do so only when the [CHARSET] is identified.

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: IMAP4rev2 implementations MUST accept and MAY transmit [UTF-8] text in quoted-strings as long as the string does not contain NUL, CR, or LF.
statements.pre_cond: quoted_string.contains_NUL = false & quoted_string.contains_CR = false & quoted_string.contains_LF = false
actions: accept UTF-8 text in quoted-strings

statements.subject: message
statements.description: A string with an excessive amount of CTL characters MAY also be considered to be binary.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Unless returned in response to BINARY.PEEK[...]/BINARY[...] FETCH, client and server implementations MUST encode binary data into a textual form, such as base64, before transmitting the data.
actions: encode binary data into a textual form such as base64 before transmitting

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Client implementations MAY attempt to create Net-Unicode mailbox names and MUST interpret any 8-bit mailbox names returned by LIST as [NET-UNICODE].
actions: attempt_create_net_unicode_mailbox_name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations MUST prohibit the creation of 8-bit mailbox names that do not comply with Net-Unicode.
actions: reject_CREATE
return_error_response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: However, servers MAY accept a denormalized UTF-8 mailbox name and convert it to Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) (as per Net-Unicode requirements) prior to mailbox creation.
actions: accept_denormalized_utf8_mailbox_name
convert_mailbox_name_to_NFC_prior_to_creation

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers that choose to accept such denormalized UTF-8 mailbox names MUST accept them in all IMAP commands that have a mailbox name parameter.
actions: accept_denormalized_utf8_mailbox_name_in_command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MAY refuse to create mailbox names containing Unicode CTL characters.
actions: reject_CREATE
return_error_response

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: If it is desired to export hierarchical mailbox names, mailbox names MUST be left-to-right hierarchical, using a single ASCII character to separate levels of hierarchy.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an INBOX exists for a user, it MUST appear within the user's Personal Namespace.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the typical case, there SHOULD be only one Personal Namespace per user on a server.

statements.subject: user
statements.description: To access mailboxes in the Other Users' Namespace, the currently authenticated user MUST be explicitly granted access rights.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the typical case, there SHOULD be only one Other Users' Namespace per user on a server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The namespaces a server uses MAY differ on a per-user basis.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: implementations that offer access to USENET newsgroups MAY use the "#news" namespace to partition the USENET newsgroup namespace from that of other mailboxes.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As such, server implementors MAY instead consider using namespace prefixes that do not contain the "#" character.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST send mailbox size updates automatically if a mailbox size change is observed during the processing of a command.
actions: send mailbox size update response to client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD send message flag updates automatically, without requiring the client to request such updates explicitly.
actions: send message flag update to client without awaiting explicit client request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: a client implementation MUST remember mailbox size updates.
actions: persist received mailbox size update in client state

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It MUST NOT assume that any command after the initial mailbox selection will return the size of the mailbox.
actions: rely solely on unsolicited mailbox size updates rather than inferring mailbox size from command responses

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations that send such responses MUST deal with flow control considerations.
actions: handle flow control before or during transmission of unsolicited untagged response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Specifically, they MUST either (1) verify that the size of the data does not exceed the underlying transport's available window size or (2) use non-blocking writes.
actions: verify data.size <= transport.available_window_size | apply non-blocking write discipline

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If a server has an inactivity autologout timer that applies to sessions after authentication, the duration of that timer MUST be at least 30 minutes.
actions: enforce_minimum_autologout_timer_duration(1800s)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY send another command without waiting for the completion result response of a command, subject to ambiguity rules (see below) and flow control constraints on the underlying data stream.
actions: send_next_command_without_waiting_for_completion_response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, a server MAY begin processing another command before processing the current command to completion, subject to ambiguity rules.
actions: begin_processing_next_command_before_current_completes

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: However, any command continuation request responses and command continuations MUST be negotiated before any subsequent command is initiated.
actions: complete_continuation_negotiation_before_initiating_subsequent_command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server detects a possible ambiguity, it MUST execute commands to completion in the order given by the client.
actions: execute_each_command_to_completion_in_client_given_order

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Therefore, if the client sends any command other than FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH, it MUST wait for the completion result response before sending a command with message sequence numbers.
statements.pre_cond: command.type != FETCH & command.type != STORE & command.type != SEARCH
actions: wait_for_completion_result_response
then_send_command_with_message_sequence_numbers

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client sends a UID command, it MUST wait for a completion result response before sending a command that uses message sequence numbers (this may include UID SEARCH).
actions: wait_for_completion_result_response
then_send_command_using_message_sequence_numbers

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Responses:    REQUIRED untagged response:  CAPABILITY
actions: send untagged CAPABILITY response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST send a single untagged CAPABILITY response with "IMAP4rev2" as one of the listed capabilities before the (tagged) OK response.
actions: send single untagged CAPABILITY response listing IMAP4rev2
send tagged OK response after untagged CAPABILITY

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST implement the STARTTLS (Section 6.2.1) and LOGINDISABLED capabilities on cleartext ports.
actions: advertise STARTTLS capability in CAPABILITY response
advertise LOGINDISABLED capability in CAPABILITY response

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST also implement AUTH=PLAIN (described in [PLAIN]) capability on both cleartext and Implicit TLS ports.
actions: advertise AUTH=PLAIN capability in CAPABILITY response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Since any command can return a status update as untagged data, the NOOP command can be used as a periodic poll for new messages or message status updates during a period of inactivity (the IDLE command; see Section 6.3.13) should be used instead of NOOP if real-time updates to mailbox state are desirable).
actions: issue IDLE command rather than NOOP to receive real-time mailbox state updates

statements.subject: server
statements.description: REQUIRED untagged response:  BYE
actions: send BYE untagged response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST send a BYE untagged response before the (tagged) OK response, and then close the network connection.
statements.post_cond: server.sent_BYE = true & server.sent_tagged_OK = true & connection.state = Logout
actions: send BYE untagged response
send tagged OK response
close network connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations MAY allow access to certain mailboxes without establishing authentication.
actions: permit mailbox access without requiring authentication establishment

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST always respond with a tagged BAD response when the STARTTLS command is received on an Implicit TLS port.
actions: Send tagged BAD response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a client issues a STARTTLS command, it MUST NOT issue further commands until a server response is seen and the TLS negotiation is complete.
actions: Block issuance of further commands until server response received
Block issuance of further commands until TLS negotiation complete

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In order to avoid this vulnerability, server implementations MUST do one of the following if any data is received in the same TCP buffer after the CRLF that starts the STARTTLS command:
actions: Interpret extra TCP buffer data as beginning of TLS handshake OR discard extra TCP buffer data

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once TLS has been started, the client MUST discard cached information about server capabilities and SHOULD reissue the CAPABILITY command.
actions: Discard all cached server capability information

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY advertise different capabilities and, in particular, SHOULD NOT advertise the STARTTLS capability, after a successful STARTTLS command.
actions: Advertise updated capability list reflecting post-TLS state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MAY also negotiate an OPTIONAL security layer for subsequent protocol interactions.
actions: negotiate optional security layer during AUTHENTICATE exchange

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the requested authentication mechanism is not supported, the server SHOULD reject the AUTHENTICATE command by sending a tagged NO response.
actions: send tagged NO response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server receives such a response, or if it receives an invalid base64 string (e.g., characters outside the base64 alphabet or non-terminal "="), it MUST reject the AUTHENTICATE command by sending a tagged BAD response.
actions: reject AUTHENTICATE command
send tagged BAD response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: As with any other client response, the initial response MUST be encoded as base64.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: It also MUST be transmitted outside of a quoted string or literal.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To send a zero-length initial response, the client MUST send a single pad character ("=").

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When decoding the base64 data in the initial response, decoding errors MUST be treated as in any normal SASL client response, i.e., with a tagged BAD response.
actions: send tagged BAD response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client uses an initial response with a SASL mechanism that does not support an initial response, the server MUST reject the command with a tagged BAD response.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = "Not Authenticated" & client.initial_response_provided = true & mechanism.supports_initial_response = false
actions: reject AUTHENTICATE command
send tagged BAD response

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: While client and server implementations MUST implement the AUTHENTICATE command itself, it is not required to implement any authentication mechanisms other than the PLAIN mechanism described in [PLAIN].
actions: support AUTHENTICATE command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: a server implementation MUST implement a configuration in which it does NOT permit any plaintext password mechanisms, unless the STARTTLS command has been negotiated, TLS has been negotiated on an Implicit TLS port, or some other mechanism that protects the session from password snooping has been provided.
statements.pre_cond: STARTTLS.negotiated = false & TLS.implicit_port = false & other_protection.active = false
actions: disallow plaintext password mechanisms when no protection layer is active

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server sites SHOULD NOT use any configuration that permits a plaintext password mechanism without such a protection mechanism against password snooping.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Client and server implementations SHOULD implement additional [SASL] mechanisms that do not use plaintext passwords, such as the GSSAPI mechanism described in [RFC4752], the SCRAM-SHA-256/SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS [SCRAM-SHA-256] mechanisms, and/or the EXTERNAL [SASL] mechanism for mutual TLS authentication.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD list its supported authentication mechanisms in the response to the CAPABILITY command so that the client knows which authentication mechanisms to use.
actions: include supported authentication mechanisms in CAPABILITY response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY include a CAPABILITY response code in the tagged OK response of a successful AUTHENTICATE command in order to send capabilities automatically.
actions: include CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY advertise different capabilities after a successful AUTHENTICATE command.
actions: advertise different capabilities than those advertised before AUTHENTICATE

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If an AUTHENTICATE command fails with a NO response, the client MAY try another authentication mechanism by issuing another AUTHENTICATE command.
actions: issue another AUTHENTICATE command with different mechanism

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It MAY also attempt to authenticate by using the LOGIN command (see Section 6.2.3 for more detail).
actions: issue LOGIN command

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In other words, the client MAY request authentication types in decreasing order of preference, with the LOGIN command as a last resort.
actions: retry with next preferred authentication type
fall back to LOGIN command as last resort

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Note that because the initial response is optional, the following negotiation (which does not use the initial response) is still valid and MUST be supported by the server:
actions: accept and process AUTHENTICATE command without initial response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The LOGIN command SHOULD NOT be used except as a last resort (after attempting and failing to authenticate using the AUTHENTICATE command one or more times), and it is recommended that client implementations have a means to disable any automatic use of the LOGIN command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY include a CAPABILITY response code in the tagged OK response to a successful LOGIN command in order to send capabilities automatically.
actions: include CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: clients MUST NOT use LOGIN on unsecure networks.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Unless the client is accessing IMAP service on an Implicit TLS port [RFC8314], the STARTTLS command has been negotiated, or some other mechanism that protects the session from password snooping has been provided, a server implementation MUST implement a configuration in which it advertises the LOGINDISABLED capability and does NOT permit the LOGIN command.
statements.pre_cond: session.implicit_TLS = false & session.STARTTLS_negotiated = false & session.other_snooping_protection = false
actions: advertise LOGINDISABLED capability
reject LOGIN command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server sites SHOULD NOT use any configuration that permits the LOGIN command without such a protection mechanism against password snooping.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client implementation MUST NOT send a LOGIN command if the LOGINDISABLED capability is advertised.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is not an extension known to the server, the server MUST ignore the argument.
actions: ignore unknown capability argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is an extension known to the server, and it is not specifically permitted to be enabled using ENABLE, the server MUST ignore the argument.
actions: ignore non-enabling capability argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the argument is an extension that is supported by the server and that needs to be enabled, the server MUST enable the extension for the duration of the connection.
actions: enable extension
maintain extension enabled until connection closed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the ENABLE command is successful, the server MUST send an untagged ENABLED response (Section 7.2.1), which includes all enabled extensions as specified above.
actions: send untagged ENABLED response
include all enabled extensions in ENABLED response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD only include extensions that need to be enabled by the server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST NOT issue ENABLE once they SELECT/EXAMINE a mailbox; however, server implementations don't have to check that no mailbox is selected or was previously selected during the duration of a connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When multiple ENABLE commands are issued, each corresponding ENABLED response SHOULD only contain extensions enabled by the corresponding ENABLE command, i.e., for the above example, the ENABLED response to "ENABLE c" should not contain "a" or "b".
actions: include only extensions enabled by the corresponding ENABLE command in ENABLED response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT change the CAPABILITY list as a result of executing ENABLE; that is, a CAPABILITY command issued right after an ENABLE command MUST list the same capabilities as a CAPABILITY command issued before the ENABLE command.
actions: preserve CAPABILITY list unchanged after ENABLE execution

statements.subject: server
statements.description: REQUIRED untagged responses:  FLAGS, EXISTS, LIST
statements.post_cond: server.sent_FLAGS = true & server.sent_EXISTS = true & server.sent_LIST = true
actions: send untagged FLAGS response
send untagged EXISTS response
send untagged LIST response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: REQUIRED OK untagged responses:  PERMANENTFLAGS, UIDNEXT, UIDVALIDITY
statements.post_cond: server.sent_PERMANENTFLAGS_OK = true & server.sent_UIDNEXT_OK = true & server.sent_UIDVALIDITY_OK = true
actions: send untagged OK [PERMANENTFLAGS] response
send untagged OK [UIDNEXT] response
send untagged OK [UIDVALIDITY] response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Before returning an OK to the client, the server MUST send the following untagged data to the client.
actions: send all required untagged responses before sending tagged OK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a LIST response with the mailbox name.
actions: send untagged LIST response with mailbox name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The list of mailbox attributes MUST be accurate.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server allows denormalized UTF-8 mailbox names (see Section 5.1) and the supplied mailbox name differs from the normalized version, the server MUST return LIST with the OLDNAME extended data item.
statements.pre_cond: (protocol.state = authenticated | protocol.state = selected) & server.allows_denormalized_UTF8 = true & mailbox.supplied_name != mailbox.normalized_name
actions: send untagged LIST response with OLDNAME extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When deselecting a selected mailbox, the server MUST return an untagged OK response with the "[CLOSED]" response code when the currently selected mailbox is closed (see Section 7.1).
actions: send untagged OK response with [CLOSED] response code before deselecting current mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client is permitted to modify the mailbox, the server SHOULD prefix the text of the tagged OK response with the "[READ-WRITE]" response code.
actions: prefix tagged OK response with [READ-WRITE] response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client is not permitted to modify the mailbox but is permitted read access, the mailbox is selected as read-only, and the server MUST prefix the text of the tagged OK response to SELECT with the "[READ-ONLY]" response code.
statements.pre_cond: (protocol.state = authenticated | protocol.state = selected) & client.has_modify_permission = false & client.has_read_permission = true
actions: prefix tagged OK response to SELECT with [READ-ONLY] response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Read-only access through SELECT differs from the EXAMINE command in that certain read-only mailboxes MAY permit the change of permanent state on a per-user (as opposed to global) basis.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The text of the tagged OK response to the EXAMINE command MUST begin with the "[READ-ONLY]" response code.
actions: include [READ-ONLY] response code at start of tagged OK response text

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client attempts to create a UTF-8 mailbox name that is not a valid Net-Unicode name, the server MUST reject the creation or convert the name to Net-Unicode prior to creating the mailbox.
statements.pre_cond: command.name = CREATE & mailbox_name.encoding = UTF8 & mailbox_name.valid_Net_Unicode = false
actions: reject the creation
OR convert the name to Net-Unicode prior to creating the mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server decides to convert (normalize) the name, it SHOULD return an untagged LIST with an OLDNAME extended data item, with the OLDNAME value being the supplied mailbox name and the name parameter being the normalized mailbox name.
statements.post_cond: response.type = untagged_LIST & response.contains_OLDNAME = true & response.OLDNAME_value = supplied_mailbox_name & response.name_parameter = normalized_mailbox_name
actions: return untagged LIST response
include OLDNAME extended data item
set OLDNAME value to supplied mailbox name
set name parameter to normalized mailbox name

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Mailboxes created in one IMAP session MAY be announced to other IMAP sessions using an unsolicited LIST response.
actions: send unsolicited LIST response to other IMAP sessions announcing the created mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server automatically subscribes a mailbox when it is created, then the unsolicited LIST response for each affected subscribed mailbox name MUST include the \Subscribed attribute.
actions: include \Subscribed attribute in unsolicited LIST response for each affected subscribed mailbox name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations that do not require this declaration MUST ignore the declaration.
actions: ignore the trailing hierarchy separator declaration

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server's hierarchy separator character appears elsewhere in the name, the server SHOULD create any superior hierarchical names that are needed for the CREATE command to be successfully completed.
actions: create any superior hierarchical names needed for CREATE command to be successfully completed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In other words, an attempt to create "foo/bar/zap" on a server in which "/" is the hierarchy separator character SHOULD create foo/ and foo/bar/ if they do not already exist.
actions: create each superior hierarchical mailbox that does not already exist

statements.subject: imap
statements.description: If a new mailbox is created with the same name as a mailbox that was deleted, its unique identifiers MUST be greater than any unique identifiers used in the previous incarnation of the mailbox unless the new incarnation has a different unique identifier validity value.
actions: assign unique identifiers strictly greater than any unique identifiers used in the previous incarnation of the mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The DELETE command MUST NOT remove inferior hierarchical names.
actions: retain all inferior hierarchical names of the deleted mailbox

statements.subject: server

include OLDNAME extended data item with original supplied mailbox name as value and normalized name as the name parameter

include \NoSelect attribute in LIST response
